sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5,931.4 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
Growth was front-loaded: revenue rose 104.0% in FY2017 and 64.2% in FY2021, then slowed to 0.1% in FY2023 before recovering to 16.4% in FY2024 and 10.6% in FY2025 [D36][D218][D311][D358][D406].
The FY2017 operating loss of $3,485.6 million reflected a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation tied to the CEO award and IPO-related RSUs [F12][P74].
The FY2022 loss widened to $1,395.3 million as cost of revenue and operating expenses rose faster than revenue [F17][P42].
The operating margin improved from -30.3% in FY2022 to -9.0% in FY2025, the window high [F27][F30][D554].
North America remains the largest market at 58.6% of FY2025 revenue but contributed only 4.4pp of the 10.6% growth, while Rest of world added 3.7pp [D456][D458][D499][D406].
Other revenue contributed 5.4pp of FY2025 growth, nearly matching advertising's 5.3pp, and rose to 12.6% of revenue from 4.3% in FY2023 [D545][D538][D543][D539].
Advertising revenue grew on a roughly 17% increase in impressions, partly offset by a roughly 10% lower cost per impression, while other revenue rose on subscription growth [P24].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth in FY2025, an incremental operating margin of 44.8% [D423][D406][D429].
The diluted share count rose 2.1% in FY2025, so the 35.7% smaller loss per share trailed the 34.0% smaller net loss [D425][D409][D408].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is far above the window median of -32.4% and the FY2017 low of -422.5% [F30][D555][D553].
Cost of revenue fell to 45.0% of revenue from 46.1%, adding 1.1pp to margin, while R&D at 30.2% added 1.3pp [D386][D338][D431][D387][D432].
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on the timing of marketing events and lower advertising, and R&D rose $101.9 million on product development headcount [P22][P23].
Net margin of -7.8% beat operating margin by 1.2pp, helped by $96.7 million of debt-extinguishment gains in other income [F50][F30][P18].
Interest expense rose $100.4 million on the 2033 and 2034 Notes issued in FY2025 [X100][P19].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million exceeded the $460.5 million net loss in FY2025, and free cash flow reached $437.2 million, a 7.4% margin and the window high [F80][F40][F100][D393][D560].
Operating cash flow was lifted by $1.0 billion of stock-based compensation and $163.6 million of D&A, both non-cash [P13].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A, up from 1.23x in FY2024 [F90][D392][D395][D347].
Capex is primarily improvements to leased facilities to support team workspaces [P10].
Net cash swung from $1,439.8 million in FY2021 to net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025, or -10.1% of revenue [D211][D399][D400].
That ranks at the 0th percentile against internet peers, whose median net cash is 45.0% of revenue (n=5) [D578][D579].
In February 2025 Snap repurchased $1.4 billion of notes and issued $1.50 billion of 2033 Notes, leaving long-term debt at $3,489.9 million [P1][P2][F185].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow, and the current ratio fell to 3.56x, the window low [X156][D402][F180][D565].
Snap has posted a net loss in each of the last ten years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last nine years [R2][D390].
Net cash has fallen for four straight years into net debt, and buybacks exceeded free cash flow in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [R3][R4][D307][D354][D402].
The buybacks shrink the share count but are funded partly from a shrinking liquidity base, which is the main balance-sheet risk [R4][D425].
Whether the operating margin holds above the FY2025 level of -9.0% or slips back toward the -32.4% median, reported in the FY2026 10-K [F30][D555].
Whether free cash flow stays above the FY2025 $437.2 million as capex runs at 3.7% of revenue [F100][D392].
Whether net cash returns above the FY2025 net debt of $596.3 million, given buybacks at 171.7% of free cash flow [D399][D402].
